key_insight: Full hydrogenation converts metallic irida-graphene into irida-graphane, a predicted wide-gap semiconductor with a 6.0 eV indirect band gap at the HSE06 level.
engineering_relevance: Predicted visible transparency and strong deep-ultraviolet absorption make irida-graphane a candidate for ultraviolet optoelectronics and transparent coatings.
method: PBE and HSE06 density functional theory calculations
Phonon analysis and ab initio molecular dynamics
Structural, mechanical, electronic, and optical characterization
evidence_signal: Calculations predict no imaginary phonon frequencies, structural integrity in AIMD simulations up to 2000 K, visible reflectivity below 0.3%, and deep-UV absorption coefficients of 10⁵–10⁶ cm⁻¹.
watch_item: Experimental synthesis and validation remain needed; simulated stability does not establish practical fabrication or device performance.
paper_title: First-Principles Investigation of Irida-Graphane: A Wide-Band-Gap Semiconductor Derived from Irida-Graphene
